educationalGoal:
Quantum mechanics is at the root of the latest modern technology, and quantum mechanics continues to make strong advances, including applications to quantum computers and quantum information. Even if you are not fully familiar with the mathematical aspects of modern education, it will be essential in the future to acquire the basic knowledge of quantum theory.
In this lecture, we will explain the basic content of quantum mechanics in a way that even second-year students can underst.
advice:
In this lecture, we will explain the structure of quantum mechanics and learn about its differences from classical physics. The use of mathematical formulas will be kept to a minimum, but in order to explain the structure, a minimum number of mathematical formulas will be presented, and the focus will be on explaining their physical meaning without delving into the treatment of mathematical formulas.
① Explain how quantum mechanics is constructed from classical mechanics through a procedure called "quantization." At this time, we will also explain the very basics of analytical mechanics necessary for quantization. ② Present the Schroedinger equation and explain its origin and interpretation, especially the fact that Schroedinger himself was unable to correctly interpret the equation he developed ③ Briefly explain the range of applications of quantum mechanics and explain the uncertainty principle I will explain about it. ④In addition to explaining quantum entanglement such as EPR correlation, we will also explain paradoxes such as Schroedinger's cat. ⑤Explain the interpretation of quantum mechanics. Specifically, I will explain the Copenhagen interpretation, the many-worlds interpretation, etc. Note that there are no serious textbooks that contain mathematical formulas that correspond to this lecture, so references will be introduced as appropriate.
books:
Do not use textbooks.
References will be given as appropriate in class.
requiredKnowledge: It is desirable to have basic knowledge of high school physics (especially mechanics) and basic knowledge of first-year mathematics calculus, but even if you have some gaps, you can listen to the lectures with concentration and improve your knowledge. You can take the course if you are willing to proactively research the parts you are lacking in and work on the tasks to make up for it. Even if you have a lot of prior knowledge, it will be difficult to complete the course if you are unable to maintain concentration during lectures.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the differences between classical mechanics and quantum mechanics and the "quantization"
Be able to explain the origin and interpretation of the Schroedinger equation.
Be able to explain the simple application range and uncertainty principle of quantum mechanics.
Be able to explain quantum entanglement such as EPR correlation and paradoxes such as Schroedinger's cat.
Be able to explain the interpretation of quantum mechanics.
Be able to attend every class, work on assigned assignments, and strive to understand the lesson content.
